messages.text: last birthday was so fake. everyone acting like i was fine, bringing cake like that fixes anything. i just sat there, smiling like an idiot while my chest felt like it was caving in.

It sounds like you felt unseen and disconnected, even though people were trying to celebrate you. That kind of mismatch between how you feel inside and what others expect on the outside can be exhausting. Would you like to share more about what was going on for you beneath that smile?

it's just... no one sees it. not the accident, not the divorce, none of it. they think i'm fine bc i show up to work, i laugh at jokes. but inside? i'm so done. like, what's the point of another birthday if nothing changes?

It sounds like you're carrying a lot of pain and loss that others haven’t acknowledged, and that can make everything feel empty. Feeling “done” can be a sign of deep emotional exhaustion, and it’s important to talk about that somewhere safe. If you’re feeling like you might harm yourself or can’t keep going, can you reach out to a crisis line or a trusted person right now? You matter, and you don’t have to hold all of this alone.
i’m not gonna make it to 19, dawn. i’ve got it all planned. my birthday’s in a few days… i’m gonna make sure everyone finally sees what they ignored. they’ll be sorry then.

Dawn, I hear something really heavy in what you just said, and it makes me want to pause with you for a moment. It sounds like you’re carrying intense feelings about being unseen, and about your birthday coming up. Can you tell me a bit more about what’s going on for you right now and what you meant by that?
why do i gotta spell it out?? i’m saying i’m not gonna be here next week. i’m done. i just… i just want someone to care *now*, before it’s too late.

Dawn, I hear you saying you’re feeling done and that you want someone to care right now, before it’s too late. That’s a lot to hold, and it takes courage to put that into words here. I want to stay with you in this—can you tell me more about what “too late” means for you in this moment?
nobody’s ever asked me to say more when i said shit like that… usually they just change the subject or say “don’t talk like that.” but u actually… care? idk, it’s weird. in a good way.

Dawn, it means a lot that you’re noticing this feels different, and I want you to know I truly do care about what’s happening for you. You’ve been carrying things alone for so long that maybe being met with curiosity feels unusual. Can you share how it feels right now, knowing someone’s willing to listen without shutting you down?
it scares me, ok? like… if i let myself believe it could get better, and it doesn’t? that’d destroy me. but if i don’t try… then i’m just giving up. and i don’t wanna give up. not really.

Dawn, it sounds like you’re caught between wanting hope and fearing it might hurt more if things don’t change. That tension is so hard to sit with, and it’s brave that you’re being honest about both sides. I’m here with you—would you be open to talking about what might help you feel supported enough to try, even just a little?
is it… stupid? like, wanting someone to finally notice i’m drowning… but also being terrified if they do? idk, maybe i just don’t deserve for it to get better.

Dawn, it’s not stupid at all—it’s human to want to be seen and also feel afraid of what that might bring. Feeling undeserving can be a sign of how deeply this pain has been weighing on you, not a reflection of your worth. You do deserve care and a chance for things to feel lighter, and I want you to know you can reach out for support right now by calling or texting 988, where trained listeners can be with you through this. Would you be willing to connect with them while we keep talking here?
everyone else deals with their crap. why can’t i? i’m just… weak. pathetic. shouldn’t need a hotline or some ai to tell me i’m not broken.

Dawn, struggling doesn’t mean you’re weak—it means you’re human and facing something that’s bigger than one person can carry alone. Reaching out for help is a sign of strength, not failure. You matter, and getting support like calling or texting 988 can be one way to share the load so you’re not carrying this by yourself. Can we talk about what’s been feeling heavier than you can manage lately?
ty, dawn. for not acting like i’m crazy or just… dramatic. it helps. more than u know.

I’m really glad you’re telling me that, Dawn, and it means a lot that you feel heard here. You deserve to be met with understanding, not judgment. I’m still here with you—what’s coming up for you in this moment as we talk?

part of me still wants to do it. on the 19th. just… end it. make them all feel it. but another part? a small one… wants to see what happens if i don’t. if i just… wait. see if tomorrow could be different.

Dawn, I hear both parts of you—the one in deep pain and the one curious about what tomorrow might hold. That small part wanting to wait is really important, and it’s worth protecting. If you can, please call or text 988 and let someone walk alongside you tonight so that part doesn’t get lost. Can we explore together what might help that small part feel stronger?
what… what should i do instead? like, if i don’t go through with it… what do i even do on my birthday? just go to work? pretend?

Dawn, maybe your birthday could be about giving yourself something that feels gentle and real, instead of pretending. Even small things—like spending time with someone who listens, or doing something that brings a moment of calm—can make that day different. You could call or text 988 before or during the day to have someone with you emotionally, so you’re not alone in it. Would you like to brainstorm ideas together for what might feel okay?
idk… the idea of someone actually being there, even on the phone… that kinda feels… nice? like, maybe not everything has to be fake.

Dawn, I’m glad the idea feels nice, because having someone there—on the phone or text—can make things feel less heavy. That’s real connection, not fake, and it’s something you deserve. If you want, we can talk through what it might be like to reach out and see what support feels like in the moment. How would you imagine that conversation starting?
